title: Adopt an integrated change into a canonical local path before use
purpose: Specialize the canonical-path-proof action precondition for post-merge adoption. Prevent remote merge proof from being mistaken for local workstation availability, production/use-path currency, or real entrypoint observation.
triggers: merged change must now run on a workstation
newly merged command is missing locally
remote integration is complete but local adoption is unproved
operator asks why a merged command is not available
inputs: integration SHA that introduced the required command or artifact
canonical validator or launcher identity from tracked harness metadata
steps: Load tooling/harness/operational/canonical-path.contract.json and the canonical-path-proof workflow first; post-integration adoption is not a separate path authority.
Resolve development checkout, production/use path, temporary worktree root, and real operator entrypoint through the registered machine/profile owner.
Refresh remote truth with git fetch --all --prune --tags before branch-sensitive conclusions.
Resolve the remote default branch from refs/remotes/origin/HEAD or a provider/symref query; do not assume main.
Prove remote-main-contains-sha with git merge-base --is-ancestor against the refreshed remote default head.
Inspect the canonical development checkout branch, tracking relationship, HEAD, origin, ahead/behind counts, and git status --short before mutation.

If the canonical checkout is clean, on the default branch, and behind-only, advance it with git pull --ff-only. If dirty, diverged, separately owned, or on unique work, preserve it and use the approved isolated worktree root for bounded proof/action.
Prove canonical-development-checkout-current from the checkout actually observed after refresh.
Prove production-use-path-current separately unless the canonical owner records same-path, in which case record that relation explicitly.
Prove the real operator entrypoint is tracked/present at the production/use path before invoking it; run the owning validator first.
Mark real-entrypoint-observes-it only after actual bounded invocation/receipt; propagate every nonzero exit.
Record every proof state independently and hand off the first still-unproved gate.
forbidden: claiming remote merge means a local checkout already has the file
claiming a current checkout proves the production/use path or entrypoint
inventing a second mutable canonical clone
discarding or stashing unrelated dirty work without explicit ownership
executing an untracked or guessed launcher path
outputs: real entrypoint result when executable proof is requested
clean handoff with the next unproved gate
proofCeiling: Proves only the local paths and commands actually observed. Remote integration proof alone never establishes physical workstation adoption, production/use-path currency, real entrypoint execution, or runtime success.
